name: Amazon Nova 2 Sonic
access: Amazon Bedrock (InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream on the bedrock-runtime endpoint; model id amazon.nova-2-sonic-v1:0; Regions us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-north-1 and ap-northeast-1)
Amazon Connect (also Asia Pacific (Singapore), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul) and Europe (Frankfurt))
Integrations the Nova 2 guide describes: Strands Agents, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, LiveKit, Pipecat and telephony providers

voice.input_audio: Linear PCM (audio/lpcm), 16-bit, mono, sent as base64 in audioInput events. Sample rate 8,000, 16,000 or 24,000 Hz. Frames of about 32 ms from the microphone [nova2-sonic-input-events]
voice.output_audio: Linear PCM (audio/lpcm), 16-bit, mono, base64, at 8,000, 16,000 or 24,000 Hz as chosen in promptStart. AWS marks all generated audio with an inaudible watermark [nova2-sonic-input-events, nova2-service-card]
voice.voices: 16 voice IDs on the language-support page and in the promptStart schema: tiffany, matthew, amy, olivia, kiara, arjun, ambre, florian, beatrice, lorenzo, tina, lennart, lupe, carlos, carolina and leo. Tiffany and Matthew are polyglot voices that speak every supported language. The service card says eighteen voices in one sentence and twenty-two in another [nova2-sonic-languages, nova2-sonic-input-events, nova2-service-card]
voice.turn_detection: Server side. sessionStart takes turnDetectionConfiguration.endpointingSensitivity: HIGH (pause of 1.5 seconds), MEDIUM (1.75 seconds, the recommended default) or LOW (about 2 seconds) [nova2-sonic-turn-taking, nova2-sonic-input-events]
voice.interruption: Barge-in is supported. The model stops generating, keeps the conversation context and sends an interruption signal. Audio is generated faster than it plays, so the client must clear its playback queue at once [nova2-sonic-barge-in, nova2-sonic-output-events]
voice.latency: AWS says its March 2026 refresh cut user-perceived latency at the 50th percentile by 150 ms and gives no absolute figure [nova2-release-notes]. Artificial Analysis measured 1.14 seconds average time to first audio on its Big Bench Audio set [aa-speech-to-speech]. A consultancy's AWS-blog write-up reports 1.39 seconds on the same set [aws-blog-voice-agent].
voice.session_limit: A connection lasts at most 8 minutes. The client renews the connection and continues the conversation with saved chat history, which can be 200 KB in total and 50 KB a message and is sent once before audio. The default quota is 20 concurrent InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream sessions per AWS account in each Region, and AWS says the quota cannot be raised [nova2-sonic-getting-started, nova2-sonic-chat-history, bedrock-card-nova-2-sonic]

pricing_usd_per_mtok.notes: AWS Price List, Amazon Bedrock, on-demand, US East (N. Virginia), published 2026-10-03. Speech input $0.003 per 1,000 tokens ($3.00 per million). Speech output $0.012 per 1,000 ($12.00 per million). Text input $0.33 per million and text output $2.75 per million. AWS says text tokens apply to transcription, tool calls, grounding and chat history [aws-price-list, nova-pricing-page]. Other Regions: eu-north-1 speech $2.91 in and $11.65 out; ap-northeast-1 speech $3.63 in and $14.52 out; us-west-2 speech the same as us-east-1 [aws-price-list]. Artificial Analysis converts this to $0.27 per hour of input audio and $1.08 per hour of output audio [aa-speech-to-speech]. AWS does not state how many tokens one second of speech uses.

retires: no retirement is announced; the Bedrock card says end of life no sooner than 2026-12-02 with a legacy period of at least 6 months, which is a floor and not a date
context_window: the Bedrock card and the AWS announcement say 1M tokens; 1,000,000 recorded as the nearest integer
max_output: the Bedrock card says 64K without an exact figure; 64,000 recorded
released: AWS refreshed the model in place in March 2026 and from 2026-05-21 to 2026-05-28 without a new model id, so the model served today differs from the 2025-12-02 release
benchmarks: the Artificial Analysis row is the March 2026 version, taken before the May 2026 refresh; the row has no conversational dynamics or agentic value, so it has no index score
voice.voices: the service card gives eighteen and twenty-two voices; the language-support page and the promptStart schema list 16 IDs
voice.latency: AWS publishes no absolute latency figure; the figures recorded are a measurer's and a consultancy's

access: the inference page of the Nova 2 guide lists inference ids us.amazon.nova-2-sonic-v1:0 and global.amazon.nova-2-sonic-v1:0, and the Bedrock model card says geo and global inference ids are not supported
pricing_usd_per_mtok: AWS does not state how many tokens a second of speech uses, so a price per minute cannot be derived from AWS pages
